analysis.file_name: GS Vogel - MUST READ - GS 2027 Macro and Market Outlooks (part1) 15 Nov 2026.pdf
analysis.title: MUST READ - GS 2027 Macro and Market Outlooks (part1)
key_insights: Global growth was 2.7% in 2026, in line with potential. GS expects 2.8% in 2027 as lower energy prices and strong AI capex outweigh tighter financial conditions and more neutral fiscal policy. Risks are tilted to the downside: renewed Iran escalation, large fiscal deficits pushing long-term yields up (especially France), and AI capex disappointment.

GS expects two more Fed hikes (December and March) and one ECB hike, then both return to cuts in late 2027. The Fed cuts once in December 2027 and three more times in 2028, to a terminal rate of 3.25-3.5%.

US core PCE is expected to slow from 3.2% at end-2026 to 2.4% at end-2027. Tariffs still add 40bp to year-over-year core PCE through October and should drop out of the year-over-year data next spring. The Iran war's inflation boost is also expected to be much smaller.
GS sees more dovish rate risk in the US than in most economies, because US inflation drivers look more temporary and the US is most exposed to an AI-cycle downturn.

Global Markets Outlook lists 10 themes for 2027: a maturing market cycle, AI investment impulse peaking, equity gains rotating from AI infrastructure to other areas, energy risk premium, bonds regaining macro and hedging value, a more cyclical Dollar, Europe/UK pressure, financing stress for the boom, EM resilience, and tail hedges.

GS sees UST 10y yields at 4.6% by end-2027 and favors higher bond allocations on higher running yield and cheap valuations. It also expects further widening in US credit spreads, since record credit and equity issuance needs discounted pricing in credit.

GS expects the broad trade-weighted Dollar to fall roughly 3% in 2027, especially versus Asia's revaluing currencies (JPY, CNY). Near term, the Dollar is expected to strengthen somewhat further against DM currencies.

Global equity strategy (Oppenheimer): equities have de-rated sharply and are expected to keep rising with high volatility. GS is overweight the US and Japan, neutral Asia and EM, and underweight Europe. Focus areas are US Hyperscalers, AI monetisation beneficiaries, Power and Growth.

Euro area growth is forecast at 0.9% in 2027, below consensus. Headline inflation stays near 4% through the winter and core peaks at 2.9% in Q2. GS expects one more ECB hike in December and cuts from 2027Q4. French budget tensions are the main risk.

European equities: EPS growth is expected to slow to 7% in 2027 from 18% in 2026, with STOXX 600 targets of 670/680/700 at 3/6/12 months (6% price return, 9% total return over 12 months). GS recommends DAX vs SXXP and UK domestic (GSSTUKDE) vs FTSE 100, and says it is too early to re-engage with French domestic stocks (GSXEFRDO).
Japan: 12-month TOPIX target cut to 4500 from 4600. FY27/28 EPS growth is +9%/+8%, moderating from +24% in FY26.

EM equities: MSCI EM target is 1850, a 17% USD price return. Profit growth is expected to slow from 66% in 2026 to 26% in 2027 and 13% in 2028 as AI capex peaks. India, China and Mexico are raised to OW, and Taiwan is lowered.

Asia equities: the MXAPJ target is 960 (previously 1040), a 19% USD price return, or 13% excluding Korea and Taiwan. China H and India are raised to OW, Taiwan and China A lowered to MW. Korea and Japan stay OW. GS favors calls, call spreads and risk reversals on larger, more liquid markets.

FX: EUR/USD is forecast at 1.08 in 3m and 1.15 by end-2027. EUR/GBP is forecast at 0.86 and GBP/USD at 1.34 in 12m. USD/JPY is forecast at 158/155/150 in 3/6/12 months, with the BoJ expected to hike three more times by 25bp to 2% by June 2027 versus about 1.75% priced.

Commodities: GS recommends a positive allocation. 2027 average Brent is $88/bbl and TTF is 45EUR/MWh. Copper is forecast at $15,600/t and gold at $4,650/toz by Dec27. Energy hedges favored are long European summer 2027 gasoline futures and 27Q1 call spreads on European natural gas.
LatAm: LA7 growth is 1.6% in 2027, Mexico about 2.0% and Brazil 0.6%. Copom is expected to cut Selic 125bp to 12.5% and Colombia 75bp to 11.5%.

CEEMEA: GS says markets price in too much tightening in 2027, especially in CEE and South Africa. It is bullish on frontier FX (NGN, EGP, KZT) and SAGBs, and more dovish than market pricing in Poland, Czechia and Hungary.
Asia FX/rates: GS expects KRW, TWD and MYR to outperform in Asian FX, and INR among high yielders. Trades are long INR/IDR, long MYR/THB, short SGD/CNH, and INR 30Y and PHP 5Y bonds in rates.

China: real GDP growth is expected to slow to 4.5% in 2027 from 4.6% in 2026. Headline CPI is expected at 0.5% versus 1.4-1.5% in Bloomberg consensus and IMF forecasts, supporting views of falling Chinese rates and a stronger CNY.

sector_views.rationale: Long-duration Growth becomes more valuable as growth rates slow. US Hyperscalers keep strong, though slower, earnings growth and balance sheets.
Underweight on relative growth, profitability and valuation, although earnings growth of 7% and a 5.5% FCF yield are positives.
Energy EPS is expected to decline in Europe as prices ease. GS still favors asymmetric energy hedges because of escalation risk.

earnings_insights: European earnings growth is expected at 7% in 2027 versus 18% in 2026 (GS forecast), partly from lower Energy EPS.
TOPIX FY27/28 yoy EPS growth is forecast at +9%/+8% (GS forecast) versus +24% in FY26.
EM profit growth is forecast at 26% in 2027 and 13% in 2028 (GS forecast) versus 66% in 2026, as AI capex peaks. India profit growth is forecast at 15%.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Steady baseline with downside risks from Iran, French fiscal stress and AI capex.
Tariff effects drop out next spring, supporting disinflation and later Fed cuts.

risk_factors: Renewed Iran escalation could cause another energy price surge.
Large fiscal deficits could push long-term yields up sharply, especially in France.
AI capex could disappoint because of capacity constraints, regulation, credit market stress or weaker demand.
Tighter financial conditions could stall the rotation of equity gains from AI infrastructure.
Further widening in US credit spreads is likely given record issuance.
The US is most exposed to an AI-cycle downturn.
Intensifying French budget tensions are the main euro area risk.
vol_and_positioning: Equity index volatility has scope to rise further, per the Global Markets Outlook.
Global equities are expected to rise with high volatility.
GS favors calls, call spreads and risk reversals on larger, more liquid Asian markets.
Tail hedges: bonds and commodities offer diversification benefits.
geopolitical: Renewed escalation in Iran could cause another energy price surge.
The Iran war and the energy supply shock affected 2026 inflation and growth.
French budget tensions and the French election weigh on European markets and EUR.
The US-China power race creates upward price pressure in copper and gold.
Argentina's October presidential election and Mexico's June midterms are the main 2027 political events in LatAm.
cross_bank_references: GS expects China CPI of 0.5% in 2027, versus 1.4-1.5% in Bloomberg consensus and the IMF forecast.
GS rate path for the ECB is below market pricing.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong AI capex and hyperscaler earnings and balance sheets support growth and US equities, with long-duration Growth gaining value as growth slows.
tension_points.bear_case: AI capex could disappoint because of capacity constraints, regulation, credit market stress or weaker demand, and the US is most exposed to a downturn.

tension_points.bull_case: Baseline is a gradual decline in energy prices, supporting lower inflation and European equities.
tension_points.bear_case: Renewed Iran escalation could cause another energy price surge, one of the largest near-term risks.
